contract: When a user scrolls far enough in a user activity stream to load additional pages, opens a topic, and navigates back, the activity stream must return with the loaded items and scroll position needed to place the user where they were reading.
symptoms: The browser attempts to restore the previous scroll offset after Back navigation.
The activity list may be shorter after returning than it was before navigation.
The user lands substantially higher in the activity stream than the position they left.
reproduction: Open a user activity stream with enough items to trigger infinite scrolling.
Scroll until an additional page of activity has loaded.
Open a topic from deep in the loaded stream.
Use browser Back and compare the restored item set and scroll position.

runtime.notes: Discourse system tests require the repository's normal Ruby/database/browser environment. Follow the pinned repository development instructions.

validation.guidance: Add or identify a focused system test that loads more than one page, navigates away, goes Back, and asserts both retained items and restored scroll position before considering broader suites.
